content:
If you've recently purchased a new Mac, such as the newly released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you may also need to buy a new external monitor.

Below are my recommendations, covering multiple product categories, price points, and more.

The best external monitors for Mac

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to the best monitors on the market, Apple's Studio Display is a must-mention. Although it's on the pricier side, it features Apple's signature sleek design and comes with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color support: Wide color gamut (P3), supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • True Tone technology: Automatically adjusts the display's color temperature to match ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display comes in multiple configurations at different price points, detailed below. If you want an iMac-like experience with your Mac, the Apple Studio Display is the best choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR was released earlier this year and offers several major advantages over the regular Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR brightness, peak HDR brightness of 2,000 nits
  • Color support: Wide P3 and Adobe RGB color gamuts, supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 120Hz, with Adaptive Sync support
  • Host charging: Up to 140W

Of course, the price for these advantages is a higher cost compared to the regular Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor features a 4K OLED panel, making it an attractive option for Mac users. My 9to5Toys colleague Justin Kahn has switched to it, saying "it's been great paired with my Mac mini over the past few months."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2 USB-A
  • Built-in camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

Although it doesn't offer the 5K or 6K resolution of other options on the list, you can enjoy the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks and better color reproduction and contrast.

Buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K is the evolution of LG's high-end display lineup. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels. The port selection is also very generous. Here are the main specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • True Tone technology: None; supports auto brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast ratio: 2,000:1

Here are the purchase links for the LG UltraFine 6K

Asus ProArt 5K Monitor

My colleague Jeff Benjamin has hands-on experience with this unit, and I was immediately drawn to it. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K monitor offers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880) as the Studio Display, also in a 27-inch size, but at half the price.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz, with Adaptive-Sync support
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient sensing: Ambient light and backlight sensors for automatic brightness and color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: One USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode support, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

Check out Jeff's full review for all the details. If you're looking to buy a 5K monitor to pair with your Mac, the Asus ProArt is hard to beat.

Here are the purchase links for the Asus ProArt 5K monitor:

Asus ProArt 6K Monitor

If you're looking for a larger, higher-resolution option, Asus has you covered too. The brand-new Asus ProArt 6K monitor (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch display with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "absurdly good value for money" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits, peak HDR 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz, with Adaptive-Sync support (48–60Hz)
  • Webcam: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub connections, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

The biggest selling point of the ASUS ProArt 6K monitor may be its price. Compared to the most popular 4K and 5K monitors on the market, it's significantly cheaper.

Here are the purchase links for the ASUS ProArt 6K monitor:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

Samsung's ViewFinity S8 5K is another attractive option to pair with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits
  • Color support: 99% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient sensing: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness based on ambient light
  • Ports: One USB-C with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, Ethernet, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Here are the purchase links for the Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Monitor

This may currently be my favorite option. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor comes packed with Mac-friendly features, headlined by its crisp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: Typical and peak 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C, one downstream USB-C, three USB-A, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller with customizable control keys

Here are the purchase links for the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor:

In-depth review: BenQ's 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 designer monitor is a true rival to the Apple Studio Display

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Monitor

If you're looking to pair a 32-inch monitor with your new Mac for under $1,000, this is one of the most attractive options. The biggest drawback is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. However, it offers a rich selection of ports, and the 32-inch panel is priced under $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Color support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient sensing: No automatic ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C, three USB-A, USB-B, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

Here are the purchase links for the BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt monitor:

In-depth review: Are 32-inch 4K Mac monitors really not worth considering?

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultrawide Monitor

If you're looking to pair an ultrawide monitor with your Mac, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options on the market. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch display, along with plenty of ports, a matte screen, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits, peak HDR 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: Up to 120Hz, with VRR support
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient sensing: Ambient light sensor for automatic brightness and color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C, five USB-A, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Here are the purchase links for the Dell U4025QW 40-inch ultrawide monitor:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

If you want to enter the ultrawide monitor market at a more affordable price, consider the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC, which is currently selling at close to half price. While its features aren't as rich as other options, you get a 34-inch ultrawide curved display and plenty of ports, including a Thunderbolt 4 port with power delivery support.

  • Display: 34-inch ultrawide curved display with Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1000R curvature for an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits.
  • Webcam: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (providing up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0, one RJ45 Ethernet, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Here are the purchase links for the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC:

Summary

The above is just a selection of the best external monitors to pair with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, rich connectivity options, and unique sizes and form factors.

Have you recently bought a new Mac? Which monitor are you using to pair with it? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
